text:
Jordan: Pushed two variants for the first-run setup checklist: modal (center) and slide-in helper (right drawer). Figma: https://figma.com/proto/onboard-checklist-variants. Want quick calls on keyboard flow, dismiss patterns, and copy.

Maya: Nice. My gut: modal is more interruptive but forces completion. Drawer feels lighter and less scary for new users.

Ryan: If we use modal, avoid trapping keyboard unless it's a required flow. For optional checklist, prefer non-modal region or a drawer with aria-hidden toggling.

Samir: Agree. Also need to think about assistive tech: a modal should use role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" plus focus management. Drawer can be role="complementary" or a region with aria-label.

Leo: Accessibility nit: both variants must have visible focus outlines and focus order consistent across zoom/large text. Also ensure text contrast for buttons meets 4.5:1.

Casey: Copy suggestions: modal header: "Welcome to Redwood"; modal body: "Complete these quick steps to run your first sample project. Should take under 3 minutes." Primary CTA: "Run demo app" Secondary: "Skip for now"

Jordan: Good. For the drawer, headline should be shorter: "Get started" and CTA "Run demo" to keep small horizontal space.

Ryan: Behavioral question: if user clicks Skip, should we hide the banner/drawer for just the session or indefinitely? I vote session + show a small persistent help icon in the header that reopens the checklist.

Samir: Session-only is safer. Persisting permanently can annoy users. Also log events: checklist_shown, checklist_skipped, checklist_completed.

Maya: Keyboard specifics: for modal variant we need to store the element that had focus and restore it on close. For drawer, don't shift focus automatically on open; instead use aria-live to announce.

Leo: Code snippet for modal focus restore (quick):```js
const prevFocus = document.activeElement;
openModal();
modal.querySelector('[data-autofocus]')?.focus();
// on close
closeModal();
prevFocus?.focus();
```

Casey: Touch targets: CTAs and close should be 44x44 min. Close icon should have aria-label="Close setup". Also tapping outside to dismiss should be allowed for drawer but optional for modal only if it's not required.

dev-tools-bot: Lighthouse accessibility quick check: modal contrast OK, but drawer CTA #0a84ff on bg #ffffff ratio 3.8:1 -> fails for AA small text. Recommend darker CTA or larger text.

Jordan: Good catch. Will darken the CTA color. Also wondering about animation: slide-in should reduce motion if user has prefers-reduced-motion.

Ryan: Yes add CSS: @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { animation: none; }

Samir: One more: screen reader users might not want repeated announcements. If drawer auto-appears on first login, use aria-live="polite" and only fire once.

Maya: UX trade: modal forces discovery and higher completion rate, drawer is less disruptive and fits the product-first feeling. We should A/B test with 10% of new signups each and measure checklist_completion, time_to_first_request, and NPS after week 1.

Jordan: Action items: 1) Update colors for CTA per bot, 2) implement focus/restore snippet for modal, 3) make drawer non-focus-trapping with aria-live announcement, 4) add analytics events (Samir), 5) add reduced-motion preference (Ryan). I'll update Figma and queue a small HTML prototype for dev handoff.

Casey: Also add copy variant for onboarding emails that reference the checklist link in case they close it.

Jordan: Perfect. I'll loop in growth for the A/B setup. Thanks all :rocket:
